title: Failover automation rollout plan — Release 2026.02 (working)
content:
Owner: Tomáš Novák (Release Eng)  |  Working with: SRE (Rafael), Routing (Mina/Ravi), Control Plane (Ethan), Guardrails (Benji), Observability (Allison/Sergio)

Document purpose
- Define staged enablement plan for regional failover automation improvements landing in Release 2026.02.
- Make it safe-by-default: feature flags, per-tenant gating, deterministic policy eval, anti-flap, approvals (where required), and clean rollback.
- Tie each checkpoint to objective metrics so go/no-go is repeatable.

Release label / target window
- Release: 2026.02
- Proposed prod enablement window: 2026-02-10 to 2026-02-21 (weekdays only; avoid Fri 15:00+ local)
- Regions in scope for initial enablement: us-east, eu-west (primary pair), plus “observe-only” for us-west

What’s shipping (high-level)
1) Failover controller enhancements
- Dry-run mode in prod (compute recommended actions + evidence, no execution)
- Action rate limits + anti-flap timers
- Optional approval hooks for production execution
- Structured audit events for recommend/execute/rollback

2) Signal pipeline / decisioning
- Deterministic trigger signal priority (reachability > 5xx burn > tail latency burn > capacity)
- Corroboration requirements + dampening/hold-down
- Capacity headroom gating integrated into routing decisions

3) Data plane / gateway behavior
- Circuit breaker + retry budget tuning during failover
- Standardized overload response / Retry-After semantics (client backoff)
- Streaming reconnect behavior on redirect (client-facing stability)

4) Observability
- Failover dashboards (signals + outcomes) + burn-rate alert rules
- Dashboard annotations from automation events (INT-1149 follow-up)

Non-goals for this release (explicit)
- Full automation for Private deployments (docs/patterns only)
- Multi-cloud failover
- Changing contract language / SLA wording

Key feature flags (names + default)
NOTE: flag names are as implemented in redwood config; verify exact keys during final release config cut.

- failover.controller.enabled
  - Default: false in prod, true in staging
  - Meaning: controller service runs in watch mode; does not execute unless paired with execute flag

- failover.controller.mode
  - Values: disabled | dry_run | execute
  - Default: dry_run in staging; disabled in prod at release cut; move to dry_run then execute per steps below

- failover.controller.require_approval
  - Values: true/false
  - Default: true in prod (initial)
  - Approval mechanism: on-call ack via controller CLI + incident-bot confirmation

- routing.policy.signal_hierarchy.v2
  - Default: true in staging, false in prod until Step 3
  - Meaning: deterministic evaluation + priority + corroboration

- routing.capacity_signal.enabled
  - Default: true in staging, “shadow” in prod initially (collect + log, don’t gate)
  - Meaning: compute headroom; when gating enabled, blocks failover if target region lacks headroom

- gateway.failover_retry_budget.enabled
  - Default: true in staging; canary in prod (1% traffic) before expand

- streaming.redirect_reconnect_fix.enabled
  - Default: true in staging; enable in prod early (pre-requisite) to reduce customer impact during redirects

- failover.audit_events.enabled
  - Default: true in staging; true in prod once dashboards are ready (required for incident timeline + auditability)

Rollout principles
- Never introduce two new “decision-changing” pieces at once in prod.
  - Decision-changing = affects where traffic goes or when we flip.
- Start by increasing confidence: ship logging, audit events, dashboards, then dry-run, then execute.
- Keep rollback cheap: disable flags first; revert policies second; deploy rollback last.
- Use per-tenant + per-route allowlists for canary.

Pre-flight checklist (must be green before any prod change)
People/process
- INT-1142 prod change approval created + approved (includes monitoring plan and rollback steps)
- On-call primary/secondary assigned for each change window
- Comms plan confirmed (internal channels + Support heads-up)
- Runbooks updated and linked (Hosted API + controller runbook)

Systems readiness
- Dashboards live in prod and validated during a staged rehearsal
- Alert rules deployed but in “ticket only” mode for first 48 hours (no paging) unless otherwise specified
- Audit event pipeline verified end-to-end (controller -> event bus -> storage -> incident-bot)
- Feature flags wired to runtime (confirmed via config dump and a no-op change)

Quantitative gates
- Region health inputs
  - Reachability probe freshness < 30s (p95) in all target regions
  - Missing-signal rate < 0.1% of evaluations (controller NPE regression covered)
- Controller stability
  - Controller crashloop: 0 in last 24h
  - Evaluate loop latency: p95 < 2s

Rollout steps (staged enablement)

Step 0 — Release cut / deploy binaries (no behavior change)
- Date: 2026-02-10 (target)
- Changes in prod:
  - Deploy services/binaries with failover features compiled in
  - Keep failover.controller.mode = disabled
  - Keep routing.policy.signal_hierarchy.v2 = false
  - Keep capacity gating = shadow only
- Metrics to watch (4h):
  - Error rate (Hosted + Dedicated control plane), p50/p99 latency
  - Controller/region-health service CPU/mem and error logs
  - Audit event pipeline (if enabled)
- Rollback:
  - Standard deploy rollback to previous image (only if stability regression)

Step 1 — Enable observability + audit events (still no execution)
- Date: 2026-02-11
- Flip flags:
  - failover.audit_events.enabled = true
  - failover.controller.enabled = true (but mode still disabled)
- Expected effect:
  - Controller emits “heartbeat” + evaluation metadata (no recommendations yet)
  - Dashboards populate; annotations available
- Gates (24h):
  - Audit events ingestion success > 99.9%
  - Dashboard queries stable (no major cardinality blowups)
  - No paging noise increases > 20% vs baseline
- Rollback:
  - Disable audit events flag first; revert dashboard bundle if needed

Step 2 — Prod dry-run canary (recommendations only)
- Date: 2026-02-12
- Flip flags:
  - failover.controller.mode = dry_run
  - failover.controller.require_approval = true (irrelevant in dry-run but keep default)
  - Allowlist: 1–3 internal tenants + one low-risk external tenant (SRE-approved)
- What we’re validating:
  - Controller outputs: recommended action, confidence, evidence signals (as per acceptance criteria)
  - False positives: controller recommends failover during known-good periods
- Gates (48h):
  - Dry-run recommendation rate <= 1 “actionable failover” per 24h per region pair during normal ops
  - Any recommendation must include corroboration signals; “single-signal failover” count = 0
  - Evaluation-to-recommendation delay: p95 < 30s from first sustained impairment signal
- Rollback:
  - failover.controller.mode back to disabled

Step 3 — Enable deterministic signal hierarchy in prod (shadow impact first)
- Date: 2026-02-14 (avoid Fri if staffing is thin; move to 02-17 if needed)
- Flip flags:
  - routing.policy.signal_hierarchy.v2 = true, but execution still disabled
  - routing.capacity_signal.enabled = true (shadow logs + compute)
- Validation:
  - Compare v1 vs v2 decisions (log both) for 24h
  - Confirm dampening/hold-down behavior matches ADR intent (no rapid oscillation)
- Gates (24h):
  - Decision divergence explained for 100% of sampled cases (10+ samples)
  - “Would-have-flapped” cases reduced vs v1 (qualitative but must be demonstrably improved)
- Rollback:
  - routing.policy.signal_hierarchy.v2 = false

Step 4 — Execute mode for Hosted API (limited blast radius)
- Date: 2026-02-18
- Preconditions:
  - Streaming redirect reconnect fix enabled in prod (must be on)
  - Gateway retry budget tuning enabled at low % and stable
- Flip flags:
  - failover.controller.mode = execute
  - failover.controller.require_approval = true
  - Policy flip rate limits active (default safe limits)
  - Allowlist: Hosted API routes/models (start with 1–2 high-volume models and 1 low-volume model)
- Approval flow:
  - Controller posts “pending action” summary in incident-bot channel + links to dashboards
  - On-call acknowledges via CLI within 10 minutes; otherwise no execution
- Gates (during first execution window):
  - If real impairment occurs: detection-to-flip time <= 3 minutes for reachability loss; <= 5 minutes for high 5xx burn
  - Post-flip error rate returns to within 2x baseline within 10 minutes
  - No overload cascade in target region: GPU queue depth stays < critical threshold; 429/503 with Retry-After used instead of timeouts
- Rollback (in order):
  1) failover.controller.mode = dry_run (immediate stop)
  2) Revert policy flips using controller “rollback last action” (or manual routing policy edit)
  3) If still unstable, disable routing.policy.signal_hierarchy.v2

Step 5 — Expand to Dedicated (opt-in tenants only)
- Date: 2026-02-20
- Enablement:
  - Dedicated tenant allowlist only (explicit account manager + SRE approval)
  - Drain automation endpoint enabled only for selected pools; require manual approval
- Gates:
  - Drain progress metrics visible; drain completes within expected window (from capacity plan)
  - No dedicated SLO breach during test window (excluding explicit test tenants)
- Rollback:
  - Disable drain automation; revert routing; stop controller execution for Dedicated routes

Default safety limits (initial)
- Max automated policy flips per tenant: 2 per hour (hard block)
- Region-pair hold-down after execution: 30 minutes minimum before any subsequent flip
- Corroboration requirement: reachability OR (5xx burn + at least one of tail latency burn / probe degradation)
- Capacity gating: do not fail over into a region with < 20% headroom (or if queue depth above threshold for > 2 minutes)

Monitoring plan (what we stare at during rollout)
Core SLI/SLO
- Multi-region availability (Hosted + Dedicated)
- 5xx rate and 429/503 with Retry-After (by region, by route)
- Tail latency p99/p999 (by region, by route)

Failover-specific
- failover_decision_total{action=recommend|execute|rollback}
- failover_decision_latency_seconds (signal onset -> decision)
- failover_action_rate_limited_total
- failover_evaluation_missing_signal_total
- policy_flip_total (and flips per tenant)

Capacity / overload
- GPU queue depth, batch size, KV cache hit rate (as available)
- Autoscaling lag (time to add capacity)

Client experience
- Streaming disconnects / reconnect success rate (post-redirect)
- Retry storm indicators (gateway retries per request; upstream request amplification)

Go / no-go criteria (per change window)
Go if
- No new sev-2+ incidents attributable to rollout in last 24h
- All dashboards available and on-call agrees signals are readable
- Alert volume not materially worse (paging noise under control)

No-go if
- Missing-signal rate spikes (risk of controller crash or incorrect confidence)
- Policy flip rate unexpectedly high in dry-run (false positives)
- Target region headroom is low (<= 20%) or autoscaling is unhealthy
- Provider network instability ongoing (Victor confirms reachability anomalies)

Rollback plan (reference)
Immediate “stop the bleeding”
- Set failover.controller.mode = disabled (or dry_run if we still want visibility)
- Freeze automation actions (disable execute globally)

Restore traffic policy
- Revert routing policy to last known good config (stored snapshot ID in audit event)
- Confirm per-tenant routing pins (Dedicated) are intact

Post-rollback validation
- Confirm error rate and latency return to baseline
- Confirm no subsequent automatic flips (anti-flap working)
- File retro notes with exact timeline + links to audit events + dashboard screenshots

Open items / risks (as of 2026-02-05)
- INT-1149: dashboard annotations missing during previous rehearsal — must validate annotations in prod before Step 2
- Confirm final flag names in helm values (redwood-helm-charts/pr-621)
- Capacity thresholds for eu-west after failover: need signoff from Vanessa + latest headroom plan
- Support readiness: template response for “planned routing test” confusion (tie to comms playbook)

Notes to self (release eng)
- Keep a one-page “change log” during each window: what flipped, when, by whom, and what we observed.
- Don’t expand allowlist and enable execute on the same day.
- If we need to choose between fast detection and low false positives for first prod execute: bias toward fewer executes; keep approvals on.
